question.problem:
$$

Evaluate the following integral. Do not round the answer.

${\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}2\operatorname{csch}⁡(2x)\operatorname{coth}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
$$

First, we find the hyperbolic identities that correspond to the following trigonometric identities:

$$
\operatorname{cot}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x},\,\operatorname{csc}⁡x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}
$$

Using Osborn's rule, the corresponding hyperbolic identities are

$$
\operatorname{coth}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{cosh}⁡x}{\operatorname{sinh}⁡x},\,\operatorname{csch}⁡x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{sinh}⁡x}.
$$

Now, we rewrite the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}2\operatorname{csch}⁡(2x)\operatorname{coth}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x & =2{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}\operatorname{csch}⁡(2x)\operatorname{coth}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =2{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}\frac{1}{\operatorname{sinh}⁡(2x)}\cdot \frac{\operatorname{cosh}⁡(2x)}{\operatorname{sinh}⁡(2x)}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

We can solve this by substitution. Let $u=2x.$ Then,

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2\,⟹\,\text{d}u=2\,\text{d}x.
$$

Now, we fill the table for the limits of integration, according to the rule $u=2x.$

| $x$ | $\operatorname{ln}⁡2$ | $\operatorname{ln}⁡4$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $\operatorname{ln}⁡4$ | $\operatorname{ln}⁡16$ |

Now, we evaluate the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}2{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}\operatorname{csch}⁡(2x)\operatorname{coth}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡16}\operatorname{csch}⁡(u)\operatorname{coth}⁡(u)\,\cdot \text{d}u \\  & =-\operatorname{csch}⁡(u){|}_{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡16} \\  & =-\operatorname{csch}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡16)+\operatorname{csch}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡4) \\  & =-\frac{1}{\operatorname{sinh}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡16)}+\frac{1}{\operatorname{sinh}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡4)} \\  & =-\frac{1}{(\frac{16-{16}^{-1}}{2})}+\frac{1}{(\frac{4-{4}^{-1}}{2})} \\  & =-\frac{1}{(\frac{255}{32})}+\frac{1}{(\frac{15}{8})} \\  & =\frac{104}{255}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
